text:
The Director of the Julia Farr Rehabilitation Centre
299 Fullarton Road
5097

23 January, 2018

Dear Sir/ Madam, 
 Re: Mr Alex Maydew, aged 23

I am writing to transfer Mr Maydew who has been suffering from neurological dysfunction as a result of a car accident ten months ago. He requires a continuous rehabilitation program for improving his disability.

After being in coma for four months at Royal Adelaide Hospital, Mr Maydew has been cared in our facility, and has resumed his consciousness two months ago, with normal brain function except his ability to speak. He has also continuously received physiotherapy. As a result, he can now sit in a wheelchair using a computer, which might enable him to resume his study online for part-time. However, being in a nursing home has made him depressed.

Mr Maydew was a university student with a supportive family. He was perfectly healthy and physically active before the accident.  

Would you please arrange speech therapy and physical therapy for maximising his recovery? In addition, it will be beneficial for his depression if resuming his study is practically possible.  Thank you for taking over his care.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely, 
RN(177W)
